_about: Hand-built Fabula-order ground truth for the two fixture stories, written for issue #117.
docs/agents/story-authoring-eval.md §3.3 scores an extracted event list two ways: recall
against 'a hand-built event list for the source', and pairwise chronological ordering
accuracy. The fixture packages supply the first for free — their Scene Cards' required_beats
ARE the hand-built event list the rubric names, in the fixture author's own grain. What they
do not supply is the second: scene_cards are ordered by Syuzhet (narrated order), and the
Fabula order is exactly what the fixtures do not record.
So this file records one thing per fixture scene: where the events that scene depicts sit on
the story's own timeline. A ground-truth event's chronological key is rank * 1000 + its index
within the scene's required_beats (beats inside a scene are authored in order).
CONFIDENCE is not decoration. Rubric §2's whole point is that the fixtures are one valid
authoring, and the same caution applies here with more force, because a chronological order
is an interpretation of the source and parts of it are genuinely underdetermined. Only
'high' pairs carry the headline number; 'low' pairs are scored and reported separately so
the judgment is visible rather than buried in an aggregate.

notes: Lang's Cinderella is strictly linear: narrated order is chronological order, with no
flashback and no flash-forward anywhere in the 2,461 words. Rank therefore equals scene
order, and the §3.3 sub-metric 'pairs the source narrates out of order' has an empty
denominator here — it is N/A for this fixture, not a zero. The Carol carries that number.
Three story-time bands, and the band a scene belongs to is judged by WHEN THE DEPICTED
EVENTS HAPPEN, not by when Scrooge is shown them. A Stave II scene is a memory: the
showing is present, the remembered happening is past, and the happening is the Fabula
event. Same rule inverted for Stave IV, which is a conditional future.
PAST (ranks 10-30): Scrooge's boyhood, apprenticeship, and the Belle years. High
confidence — Dickens orders these explicitly and they are decades apart.
PRESENT (ranks 40-90): Christmas Eve, the night of the Spirits, Christmas Day, and Boxing
Day morning. Low confidence WITHIN the band, and the reason is worth stating rather than
hiding: the Stave III vignettes depict Christmas Day, and Stave V is Scrooge living that
same Christmas Day. The Cratchit dinner Scrooge is shown (scene_08) and Fred's party
(scene_10) are the same afternoon and evening as his own scene_19 visit. Ranking the
waking before the dinner is defensible and is what is recorded; it is not the only
defensible reading, so every within-present pair is marked low and excluded from the
headline ordering score.
FUTURE (ranks 100-150): all of Stave IV, in narrated order, which is also the order the
events would occur in — the death and its immediate aftermath, then Tim's death, then the
grave. Conditional, per Scrooge's own 'shadows of things that May be, only'.
The pairs that matter are the cross-band ones: every past scene is narrated AFTER
scene_01-03, and every future scene is narrated BEFORE scene_18-20. Those are the pairs
the source narrates out of order, they are all marked high, and they are the number worth
watching per §3.3.
